cards.title: 'Black October' AI Cyber Risk: Did Open-Weight Fear Mongers Overshoot?
cards.why_it_matters: This is a live, contested debate in AI safety about open-weight model risks — directly relevant to how you think about capability thresholds and policy implications of model releases.
cards.summary: Interconnects argues that fears around open-weight Claude Mythos being a catastrophic cyber weapon were overstated. GLM-5.3, now publicly available, is cited as the capability threshold, yet no step-change in cyber harm is evident over a month later. The piece quotes Rob Wiblin and Anthropic's Project Glasswing blog as examples of language it considers exaggerated, while acknowledging a real, ongoing rise in vulnerability disclosures.

cards.title: NVIDIA Nemotron Stack Powers a Halloween Interactive Talking House
cards.why_it_matters: A practical end-to-end showcase of NVIDIA's Nemotron Voice Agent stack — ASR, small LM, zero-shot TTS, and Audio2Face-3D — running fully offline on a single Blackwell workstation, useful for evaluating local inference pipelines.
cards.summary: A developer built 'MonsterHouse,' a Halloween garage-door character using NVIDIA Nemotron 3 ASR, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB (with a LoRA personality adapter), Magpie TTS Zeroshot, and Audio2Face-3D animating a custom Unreal Engine 5 rig. The full pipeline — including costume recognition via Nemotron Nano Omni and visitor tracking via YOLO and ByteTrack — runs on a single workstation with RTX PRO 6000 and RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell GPUs.

cards.title: Negative Log-Odds Gradients Boost LLM Data Attribution Recall by 35–72 Points
cards.why_it_matters: Data attribution and training data influence estimation are increasingly important for interpretability and data curation — this paper offers concrete, reproducible improvements over standard baselines.
cards.summary: The paper introduces CATT, a controlled benchmark using fictitious fine-tuning data for unambiguous attribution ground truth. Key findings: causal evidence within documents is highly localized, and standard cross-entropy-based averaging dilutes it. Replacing cross-entropy with negative log-odds gradients and aggregating only top-token scores improves ground-truth recall by 35–72 percentage points on CATT, and boosts counterfactual retraining performance by up to 4.9x on FTRACE-TREX.

cards.title: Neural Thickets Gains Come From Output Diversity, Not Weight-Space Geometry
cards.why_it_matters: Challenges a recently proposed hypothesis about pretrained model weight-space structure — the reframing as Perturb-Select-Vote has direct implications for inference-time compute and ensemble methods you might use in practice.
cards.summary: The paper reproduces Neural Thickets performance gains but shows the geometric 'dense expert neighborhood' explanation is unnecessary. Perturbing only a single decoder block recovers most gains; adding a random bias to output logits with a fully frozen model matches or exceeds full-weight perturbations on most reasoning tasks. The authors formalize this as Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV) and show logit-level PSV also improves vision performance under domain shift with no weight modification.

cards.title: SpecSlot: Decoupling Spectral Detail from Global Attention Sequence Length in Image Generation
cards.why_it_matters: A novel architecture idea for pixel-space diffusion/flow transformers that achieves better FID at lower FLOPs — relevant if you follow efficient generative model architectures.
cards.summary: SpecSlot expands each spatial anchor into multiple slots, each covering a disjoint DCT frequency band. Only the lowest-frequency slot participates in global attention; higher-frequency slots interact locally, keeping global sequence length fixed regardless of spectral resolution. On ImageNet-512, it improves FID by 2.84 over a FLOPs-matched JiT control with 3.9% fewer FLOPs. On text-to-image DPG-Bench, it surpasses JiT-B/8 by 1.06 at 40.6% lower forward cost.

cards.title: Propose-Filter-Release: A General DP Primitive That Scales Noise to Typical Sensitivity
cards.why_it_matters: A new general-purpose differential privacy primitive that could improve utility in DP-ML pipelines by avoiding worst-case noise inflation from outlier records.
cards.summary: PFR privately filters out atypical records before applying a release mechanism, allowing noise to be scaled to typical rather than worst-case sensitivity. It requires only a concave friendliness score and a friendly-DP release mechanism, then guarantees standard differential privacy under public conditions on record count. The framework generalizes propose-test-release and subsumes FriendlyCore, with instantiations for scalar statistics, PCA, KL divergence, graph effective resistances, and treatment-rule selection.
